title: Set 136

sentences.ko: 형네 집 마당에서 먹으려고 했는데 바람이 너무 세게 불어서 전부 다시 안으로 날라야 했어. 결국 바비큐를 통째로 형네 좁아터진 부엌에서 했지 뭐야. 근데 솔직히 그게 좀 더 재밌었어.
sentences.text: We were going to eat outside at my brother's place, but it got so windy that we had to carry everything back in, so we ended up having the whole barbecue in his tiny kitchen. And honestly, it was kind of more fun that way.

alts.text: So we were gonna eat out back at my brother's, but it got crazy windy and we had to haul it all back inside. Ended up doing the whole barbecue in his tiny kitchen. Kinda more fun that way, honestly.

We had planned to eat outdoors at my brother's home, but it became so windy that we had to carry everything back inside, so we held the entire barbecue in his very small kitchen. To be honest, it was rather more enjoyable that way.

sentences.note: **ended up** 는 계획과 다르게 결국 ~하게 됐다는 뜻이에요. **kind of more fun** 처럼 kind of 를 붙이면 말투가 부드러워져요.

sentences.ko: 드디어 잠들었나 싶어서 살금살금 나가려고 할 때마다 바닥이 삐걱거려서 애가 벌떡 일어나 앉는 거야. 그래서 결국 애 방 바닥에 한 시간쯤 누워 있었어. 겨우 빠져나왔을 땐 너무 지쳐서 저녁 먹을 힘도 없었어.
sentences.text: Every time I thought he was finally asleep and tried to sneak out, the floor would creak and he'd sit right up, so I ended up lying on his floor for like an hour. By the time I got out, I was too tired to even eat dinner.

alts.text: I'd think he was finally out, try to sneak off, and the floor would creak and he'd pop right up. So I just lay on his floor for like an hour. By the time I got out I was too wiped to even eat.

Each time I believed he had finally fallen asleep and attempted to leave quietly, the floor would creak and he would sit straight up, so I remained lying on his floor for about an hour. By the time I left the room, I was too exhausted even to eat dinner.

sentences.note: **sneak out** 은 들키지 않게 살짝 빠져나가다라는 뜻이에요. **the floor would creak** 의 would 는 매번 그랬다는 반복을 나타내요.

sentences.ko: 나 진짜 뭐가 열받는지 알아? 걔가 내 아이디어를 자기 것처럼 회의에 들고 갔어. 나중에 내가 한마디 했더니 내가 쪼잔하게 군다는 식으로 나오더라. 그래서 이제 나만 이상한 사람 됐어.
sentences.text: You know what really gets me? She took my idea into the meeting like it was hers, and when I said something about it afterward, she acted like I was being petty. So now I'm the one who looks bad.

alts.text: Wanna know what really bugs me? She took my idea into the meeting like it was her own, and when I brought it up after, she acted like I was being petty. So now I'm the bad guy.

Would you like to know what truly bothers me? She presented my idea at the meeting as though it were her own, and when I raised the matter afterward, she behaved as if I were being petty. As a result, I am now the one who appears to be at fault.

sentences.note: **really gets me** 는 정말 거슬리다, 열받게 하다라는 뜻이에요. **petty** 는 사소한 걸로 쪼잔하게 군다는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 네가 말해 준 그 가게 드디어 가 봤는데, 네 말이 맞더라. 파스타 진짜 맛있었어. 근데 자리 나기까지 거의 한 시간을 기다려서, 다음엔 아마 평일 저녁에 갈 것 같아.
sentences.text: We finally tried that place you told us about, and you were right, the pasta was amazing. But we waited almost an hour for a table, so next time I'd probably go on a weeknight.

alts.text: Finally hit up that place you told us about. You were so right, the pasta was insane. Waited like an hour for a table though, so next time I'd go on a weeknight.
We finally visited the restaurant you recommended, and you were correct; the pasta was excellent. However, we waited nearly an hour for a table, so next time I would likely go on a weeknight.

sentences.note: **weeknight** 는 평일 저녁을 말해요. casual 의 **hit up** 은 어떤 가게에 가 보다라는 구어 표현이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 일요일에 집 밖으로 한 발짝도 안 나갔는데, 딱 그게 필요했던 거였어. 폰은 다른 방에 두고 거의 하루 종일 소파에서 책만 읽었어. 막상 쉬어 보니까 그제야 내가 얼마나 지쳐 있었는지 알겠더라.
sentences.text: I didn't even leave the house on Sunday, and it was exactly what I needed. I left my phone in the other room and just read on the couch most of the day, and I didn't realize how tired I was until I actually stopped.

alts.text: Stayed in all Sunday and it was so what I needed. Phone in the other room, just me and a book on the couch most of the day. Didn't know how tired I was till I actually stopped.

I did not leave the house at all on Sunday, and it was exactly what I needed. I left my phone in another room and spent most of the day reading on the sofa, and I did not realize how tired I was until I actually stopped.

sentences.note: **exactly what I needed** 는 딱 필요했던 거였다는 뜻이에요. **didn't realize ~ until** 은 ~하고 나서야 비로소 알았다는 표현이에요.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

reviewed: 2번 casual 이 text 와 똑같이 Every time I 로 시작해서, 앞부분이 겹치지 않게 I'd think he was finally out 으로 시작하도록 다시 썼습니다.
4번 casual 이 text 의 두 번째 문장(But we waited almost an hour for a table)을 거의 그대로 옮겨서, 더 짧고 줄인 구어로 다시 썼습니다. note 의 hit up 은 그대로 살렸습니다.
5번 casual 이 Didn't even leave the house Sunday 로 text 앞부분과 겹쳐서, Stayed in all Sunday 로 시작하게 바꾸고 둘째 문장도 줄였습니다.
